paper.title: ClawGUI: A Unified Framework for Training, Evaluating, and Deploying GUI Agents
paper.central_claim: A unified open-source full-stack GUI framework closes training-infrastructure, reproducible-evaluation and deployment gaps, with parallel virtual/physical-device RL, dense process supervision, standardized evaluation achieving 95.8% reproduction, and personalized hybrid GUI/CLI deployment; ClawGUI-2B improves MobileWorld GUI-only success from 11.1% to 17.1%.

evidence.quote: ClawGUI-RL adopts a two-level reward formulation combining a binary outcome reward with a dense process reward.
evidence.support_explanation: Actual reward signal construction, not an autonomous architecture-improvement loop.

evidence.quote: After each action, the PRM receives the previous screenshot, the current screenshot, and the full history of actions taken so far
evidence.support_explanation: Privileged training-time judge observes transition and history; its correctness is an assumption, not established by this description.

evidence.quote: We train ClawGUI-2B based on MAI-UI-2B
evidence.support_explanation: Same-base initialization, training setup 64 environments/8 A6000/3 epochs, Qwen3.5-72B PRM.

evidence.quote: We set the maximum number of interaction steps to 50 for all evaluations.
evidence.support_explanation: Online MobileWorld GUI-only split with 117 tasks and shared declared cap; no unseen-app split demonstrated.
Author-reported 17.1 vs MAI-UI-2B 11.1; +6.0 percentage points, not +6% relative. No run performed by this reviewer.
14.5 vs GiGPO dense 17.1 changes reward AND estimator; cannot isolate PRM or infrastructure management.

evidence.quote: A result is considered successfully reproduced
evidence.support_explanation: Reproduction rule is <=2 absolute percentage-point difference OR reproduced >= official; upward deviations count automatically, so not symmetric numerical equivalence.
Author reproduction denominator explicit; not 95.8% task success or reviewer reproduction.

evidence.quote: the top- k k most semantically similar memories are retrieved and injected into the system context
evidence.support_explanation: Persistent memory implementation described, but no later-task benefit experiment found in complete paper.

evidence.quote: a point-in-box judge for standard GUI grounding benchmarks
evidence.support_explanation: Static grounding judges and OSWorld-G refusal-aware/AndroidControl action judges differ from task-completion validation.

evidence.quote: Human Review : part of the traces are further inspected by annotators
evidence.support_explanation: Prior UI-TARS already collected, filtered and trained on online traces on hundreds of PCs; does not prove all targeted infrastructure already open.

evidence.quote: AndroidWorld provides reward signals primarily by managing application state
evidence.support_explanation: Existing resettable Android benchmark and state-checker ancestor; screenshot-only real-device judging has weaker hidden-state access.

gap.author_gap: Open training infrastructure, unstable environments, inconsistent GUI evaluation and user deployment/personalization are disconnected.
gap.checked_gap: Reset/verification reliability and numerical protocol drift are concrete. Existing UI-TARS and AndroidWorld establish important online-training/reset/checker ancestry. Strong first-open-infrastructure claim cannot be verified from fixed closest-neighbor package.

reason: Scientific initial review complete except independently verified closest-neighbor gap. Fixed shared package lacks MAI-UI/GiGPO originals; controller declined unilateral expansion. G unknown, raw/display null; no production calibration claim.
rationale: Useful integrated engineering with a concrete online policy result, but author claims exceed isolated evidence. The14.5→17.1 arm confounds PRM and estimator;17.1 vs11.1 is6pp, not6% relative.46/48 uses a one-sided reproduction predicate. Memory/real-device reliability is described, not experimentally established. Missing closest-neighbor materials remain genuine unknowns rather than negative novelty evidence.
